main_text.p: pisse[?], omnem spem commeatuum ex continente Carthaginiensibus abscidisse: cuncto autem vere in castra ad Carthaginem regressum Byrsam arcem & portum, cui Cothoni nomen, simul esse aggressum, & decepto Asdrubale Carthaginiensium supremo duce, partem portus murumque ejus urbi praecinctum per C. Lælium occupasse: atque inde ipsum, in forum portui proximum perrupisse, & in eo ob ingruentes jam tenebras armatum cum omnibus pernoctasse, & cum vix diluxisset, quater mille recentes milites eodem venire jussisse: hos Apollinis fanum, quod illic erat ditissimum, ingressos, statuam ejus auratam, & cellam interiorem bracteis aureis pondo mille talentorum undequaque incrustatam in prædam vertisse, eamque ensibus secuisse, nequicquam prohibentibus præsectis: tum prædâ divisa ad reliqua agenda perrexisse: Scipionem interea in Byrsam urbis partem munitissimam, in quam civium plurimi, velut in arcem, confugerant, contendisse: ascensus in eam acclives fuisse tres, singulos domuum sublimium, contignationum senum seriâ densâ utrimque septos, e quibus Romani in arcem enisuri telis omnis generis desuper feriebantur. Pergit de-

page.notes: The catchword "inde" is the start of the next page's word "deinde", split at the line end as "de-". The first word of the page is a fragment, "pisse", read as the end of "posse" or a similar word; the letters are unclear. The show-through below the text (mirrored lines such as "ceria" and "inde") was left out. The page number "92" is partly worn and read from the shape of the digits.
